diagram_math_checks.check: Computed image boundary rays of (1,0),(0,1) by s(x,y)=(-x,x+y), t(x,y)=(x+y,-y), applying words rightmost first. C has rays (1,0),(0,1); sC: (-1,1),(0,1); stC: (-1,1),(-1,0); stsC: (0,-1),(-1,0); tsC: (0,-1),(1,-1); tC: (1,0),(1,-1). Each plotted label lies strictly between its two rays, in agreement with Verification 1.1 and the left action definition.

C intersect sC is the positive vertical ray including 0; C intersect tC is the positive horizontal ray including 0, by the computed boundaries or direct nonnegativity under s/t. Item Verification 1.2 and local stabilizer theorem (4) give {1,s} on the open vertical ray and {1,t} on the open horizontal ray. Verification 2.1 gives trivial stabilizer at q=(1,1) and W at 0. Independently enumerating 1,s,t,st,ts,sts with the displayed action reproduces all four point stabilizers.

Directly s fixes a and interchanges b,c; t interchanges a,b and fixes c. Thus these three plotted points are exactly the orbit, as in Verification 2.2, and only a lies in C. No arrows assert further transitions. Axes are explicitly not a claim of ordinary Euclidean mirror symmetry.
